verdicts.reason: A scatters the elements: the headline is centred, the CITRINE wordmark is stacked under it, the 'Find a Store' pill hangs at the bottom-left jammed against the bottom edge and off any shared axis, and the product is pushed alone to the right, so there is no left-to-right reading order. B reads as a proper banner (product, then headline over the wordmark, then CTA) on one horizontal axis, but the product pack is tiny and illegible, and the CTA crowds the right edge.

A is the same broken layout as pair 1A: the CTA is stranded at the bottom-left and nearly clipped by the bottom edge, and the headline, CTA and product share no alignment. B has a clean product → headline/wordmark → CTA flow with the CTA vertically centred, though the product label is unreadable at this size and the dead space between the elements makes the groups feel loose.

A repeats the misplaced bottom-left CTA hugging the edge and the unaligned scatter. B reads left to right with the headline and wordmark first, then the product, then the CTA, but the headline is jammed against the left canvas edge with almost no margin, the tiny product is wedged in the middle, and the right-hand gap before the CTA is uneven. It is still the clearer of the two.
